tool.title: Instant Surrender Value Calculator
tool.results_warning_body: Surrendering a policy almost always results in a financial loss compared to holding it to maturity. This calculator is for informational purposes to help you understand the potential payout. The cash surrender value of a life insurance policy in India is often lower than total premiums paid.

sections.title: What is LIC Policy Surrender Value?

content.text: The surrender value is the amount you receive from LIC if you decide to terminate your policy before its maturity date. The 'surrender value meaning in LIC' context is this cash payout. To have any surrender value eligibility, you must have paid premiums for at least two consecutive years. There are two types of surrender values:

items: Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV): This is the minimum amount LIC guarantees to pay. It is calculated as a percentage of total premiums paid plus a percentage of vested bonuses. It's the absolute floor amount.

Special Surrender Value (SSV): This is a non-guaranteed, higher value that LIC may pay, and it is the amount you will typically receive. It depends on factors like the policy term, premiums paid, and LIC's business performance. Our calculator provides an estimate for this, which is always higher than or equal to the GSV.

sections.title: How to Calculate LIC Surrender Value (Formula & Examples)

content.text: The calculation involves two main components. Here’s a simplified breakdown of the LIC surrender value formula to help you understand the logic behind our calculator:

content.title: Step 1: Calculate Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV)
content.text:
GSV = (Total Premiums Paid × GSV Factor) + (Vested Bonus × Bonus Surrender Value Factor).
The factors are determined by LIC. For example, to find the LIC surrender value after 5 years, the GSV factor might be around 50% and the bonus factor around 17%.

content.title: Step 2: Estimate Special Surrender Value (SSV)
content.text: The SSV formula is more complex: (Paid-up Value + Vested Bonus) * SSV Factor. The 'Paid-up Value' is (Sum Assured * No. of Years Paid / Total Term). The SSV factor is a variable multiplier determined by LIC. Our calculator estimates this value to give you a more realistic payout figure.

sections.title: Tax Implications of Surrendering an LIC Policy

content.text: Many people ask, 'Is LIC surrender value taxable or not?'. The tax treatment of the surrender amount is a critical factor and depends heavily on when you surrender.

items: If Surrendered After 5 Years: If you surrender the policy after paying premiums for five full years, the surrender value you receive is generally tax-free under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act, provided other conditions are met.

If Surrendered Before 5 Years: This is where it gets tricky. If you surrender before completing five premium-paying years, the tax benefits you claimed earlier are reversed. The entire surrender amount can be added to your income and taxed. Furthermore, any deductions you claimed under Section 80C for the premiums paid in previous years become taxable in the year of surrender.

content.title: Taxability Example (Surrender in Year 3):
content.text: Suppose you paid a premium of ₹50,000 each year and claimed a ₹50,000 deduction under 80C for two years. If you surrender in the 3rd year, the surrender amount may be added to your income. Additionally, the ₹1,00,000 you claimed as a deduction would be added back to your taxable income for the year of surrender.
The surrender value isn't a random number; it's influenced by several key LIC surrender value factors:

items: Policy Term & Years Completed: The longer you've paid premiums, the higher the surrender value factor. Early years yield very low returns, but the value grows significantly as you approach maturity. For example, the LIC surrender value after 3 years is much lower than the LIC surrender value after 10 years.
Premium Amount: A higher total premium paid naturally results in a higher absolute surrender value.
Accrued Bonuses: The vested bonus is a key part of the SSV. More bonuses mean a higher payout, and this 'surrender value bonus LIC' component can be significant in later years.
Policy Type: Endowment plans like Jeevan Anand, Jeevan Labh, or a New Endowment Plan have surrender values. Pure term plans do not.

sections.title: Pros and Cons of Surrendering an LIC Policy

content.text: Deciding to surrender a policy is a major financial step. Here is a balanced overview to help you decide if you should surrender your LIC policy.

rows: Instant Liquidity: You get cash to meet an urgent need.
Significant Financial Loss: You often get back much less than you've paid, especially in the early years.
Stops Premium Payments: Relief if you can’t afford them.
Loss of Life Cover: You forfeit the primary benefit of the policy—the life insurance protection for your family.
Reallocation of Funds: Allows you to move money from a low-return policy to higher-growth investments.
Higher Cost of New Insurance: If you seek new insurance later, it will cost more due to your increased age. A surrendered policy cannot be reinstated.

sections.title: LIC Surrender Value vs. Paid-Up Value

content.text: Understanding the difference between surrendering a policy and making it paid-up is crucial. They are two very different options.

items: Surrender Value: This is the lump-sum cash amount you get if you decide to completely terminate your policy before its maturity date. You lose all life cover and future benefits.

Paid-Up Value: If you stop paying premiums after a minimum period (e.g., 2 years), your policy is not terminated. It continues with a reduced Sum Assured. You don't have to pay any more premiums and will still receive this reduced maturity amount at the end of the policy term.

content.title: Pro Tip
content.text: When to Choose Paid-Up: If you cannot afford future premiums but don't need immediate cash, making the policy paid-up is almost always the better financial decision. It keeps your life insurance cover (albeit reduced) and allows your accumulated bonuses to continue earning interest.
When to Consider Surrender: Only consider surrendering if you have a dire, immediate need for cash. Remember that the surrender value vs maturity amount is always significantly lower.
Surrendering should be your last resort. Before you terminate your policy, consider these smarter alternatives:

items: Make the Policy Paid-Up: If you can no longer afford premiums, stop paying after 2-3 years. The policy continues with a reduced sum assured. This is often better than outright surrender if you don't urgently need cash.
Take a Policy Loan from LIC: For short-term needs, you can borrow against your policy’s surrender value. This provides liquidity without terminating your life cover.

Switch to a Term Plan + Invest Difference: If low returns are the issue, a better strategy is to buy a pure term insurance plan for adequate cover (much cheaper premium) and invest the remaining money in higher-return instruments like mutual funds. This often yields better results in the long run.

Continue or Partial Surrender: If it’s a money-back or ULIP, perhaps you can withdraw some bonus or use partial withdrawal options instead of full surrender (if applicable).

sections.title: How to Surrender Your LIC Policy (Process & Documents)

content.text: If you've weighed the options and still wish to proceed, here are the LIC policy surrender process steps:

items: Check Eligibility: Confirm you've met the minimum premium payment period (usually 2-3 years).
Collect Documents: Gather the documents required for LIC policy surrender: Original policy bond, a filled Surrender Form No. 5074, a copy of your PAN and Aadhaar cards, and a cancelled cheque.
Visit LIC Branch: The policyholder must visit the servicing LIC branch to submit the surrender request.
Verification & Payment: LIC will process the request, and the surrender value is usually credited via NEFT to your bank account within 7-10 working days.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) about LIC Surrender Value

content.text: Below are answers to common questions policyholders ask about surrendering LIC policies:

items.q: How do I calculate the surrender value of my LIC policy?
items.a: The surrender value is the higher of the Guaranteed (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV), calculated based on premiums paid and policy duration. Use our online calculator above for an instant, accurate estimate.

items.q: After how many years can I surrender an LIC policy?
items.a: Most LIC policies can be surrendered only after premiums have been paid for at least two to three full years. Before this, the policy has no surrender value. Some single-premium policies can be surrendered sooner.

items.q: Is the surrender value of an LIC policy taxable?
items.a: The payout is generally tax-free under Section 10(10D) if surrendered after 5 years. If surrendered before 5 years, the amount can become taxable, and any 80C deductions you've claimed may be reversed.

items.q: How much money will I get if I surrender my LIC policy?
items.a: The amount is a percentage of total premiums paid, increasing over time (e.g. ~30% after 3 years, increasing over time). Use our calculator above to get an exact estimate for your policy.

items.q: What is the difference between guaranteed and special surrender value?
items.a: GSV is the minimum guaranteed amount based on premiums paid. SSV includes a portion of vested bonuses and is calculated if bonuses are vested. LIC will pay whichever amount is higher.

items.q: Should I surrender my LIC policy or make it paid-up?
items.a: If you don’t need immediate cash and want to retain some insurance, making it paid-up can be wiser (no further premiums, reduced cover remains). Surrender is suitable if you urgently need funds or want to stop losses on a poor-return policy.

items.q: Can I surrender my LIC policy online?
items.a: No, as of now, a full surrender requires a physical visit to your LIC servicing branch with the necessary documents, though forms may be available online.

items.q: What documents are required to surrender an LIC policy?
items.a: You will need the Original Policy Bond, a filled Surrender Form (No. 5074), your PAN card, Aadhaar card, and a cancelled cheque for your bank details.

items.q: How long does it take to receive the surrender value amount?
items.a: After approval, it typically takes 5-10 working days for LIC to credit the amount to your bank account via NEFT.

items.q: Can a surrendered LIC policy be reinstated or revived?
items.a: No, once you surrender and take the money, the policy is terminated permanently and cannot be revived. One would have to buy a new policy if needed.

items.q: Do term insurance policies have surrender value?
items.a: Generally no – pure term plans usually don’t offer any payout on cancellation as they are risk-cover only. If the user has a term plan with a return of premium rider, that’s a different scenario, but standard term = no surrender value.

items.q: Will I get the bonus and loyalty additions if I surrender the policy?
items.a: Any accrued regular bonus is typically considered in the Special Surrender Value calculation, so if your policy has bonuses, the surrender value will include a portion of them. Loyalty additions might be forfeited if policy not run full term.

sections.title: Conclusion and Next Steps: Make an Informed Decision

content.text: Surrendering an LIC policy is a significant decision. You now understand the surrender value formula, the pros and cons, and the key alternatives. Use our LIC surrender value calculator online to get a clear, personalized estimate. Weigh your options carefully; a loan against policy or making it paid-up is often a better choice.
